chunk_findings.detail: When `_note_degraded` is called with `extra_evidence=None` (a case the function explicitly handles), the line `if extra_evidence is None: extra_evidence = {}` rebinds only the local name. The `"review_degraded"` entry is appended to this new local dict and then discarded on return; the caller's `extra_evidence` remains `None`, and the mark never reaches `_gate_outcome` or `degraded_marks(st)`. Concrete failure: the first reviewer to hit a quota wall in a review pass that starts with no evidence dict is announced as “marked degraded” but not actually recorded, so the next gate does not shed it and the same exhausted reviewer is selected again.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/run.py:_note_degraded

chunk_findings.detail: The regex alternative `limit(?:\s+is)?\s+(?:reached|exceeded)` matches token/context-size truncation, not just reviewer account quota walls. For example, `classify_exhaustion("max_tokens limit exceeded: output truncated")` returns `"limit exceeded"`, and `runner._settle` then sets `ReviewResult.degraded`. That makes a chunk that is merely too large for the model's token budget get shed to a different endpoint instead of being retried in halves, contradicting the adjacent comment explicitly excluding `_truncated`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/model.py:_EXHAUSTION_RE

chunk_findings.detail: The intent for B8efd3d1bc4 explicitly lists “qwen truncation” as one of the quota walls that must trigger automatic failover. This test asserts `classify_exhaustion("TRUNCATED: the model consumed all 16000 tokens") == ""` and says “NEVER shed for these.” Given an exhausted qwen cross-family reviewer that emits that truncation, the classifier returns no degradation reason, so the reviewer is not marked/shed and the gate still stalls—the exact bug remains. The test should expect a degradation reason for the qwen truncation shape, not `""`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_quota_failover.py:76

chunk_findings.detail: When `extra_evidence` is None and `res.degraded` is set (for example `"quota"`), the `if extra_evidence is None: extra_evidence = {}` branch rebinds only the local name, appends the mark to that discarded dict, and returns nothing. The caller still holds None, so the quota/exhaustion record never lands on the gate outcome. The console line still claims the reviewer was marked and shed, but the evidence the rest of the run persists is unchanged — the same silent drop this change is meant to stop.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/run.py:_note_degraded

chunk_findings.detail: `_EXHAUSTION_RE` is unanchored and treats any `quota` substring or `limit … exceeded/reached` as the reviewer’s own account wall. `classify_exhaustion("token limit exceeded")` returns `"limit exceeded"`, and `classify_exhaustion("quotation")` returns `"quota"`, so `_settle` sets `ReviewResult.degraded` and the shed path drops a healthy endpoint. Those strings are the diff-shape / truncation cases the comment on the same regex says must not failover (chunk halving), not an HTTP 403/429 account wall.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/model.py:278

data.summary: The generic orchestrator should be a ddflow-native scheduler that MONITORS implement status (lane liveness, INTERRUPTED, ready-set, completion) and ACTS (fill/refill/recover/complete) as a loop extending /implement and the lanes-watchdog watch+signal, so the driver is ddflow itself. Today the watchdog act mode is per-decision default-off and the fill/recover/complete loop lives in the harness Kilo cron instead, so there is no in-repo scheduler: implement the native scheduler loop (extend /implement to a claim-implement-gates-merge-complete-next loop plus a monitor that fills idle lanes/reaps interrupted/accepts red), keeping refill demoted to the harness wave-driver per the autofill-is-harness-pattern decision. Natural extension of B4e2a112a97.
data.title: the implement-status scheduler is not a ddflow-native loop; the harness cron substitutes

data.body:
Fixes bug Bd43790a326: The generic orchestrator should be a ddflow-native scheduler that MONITORS implement status (lane liveness, INTERRUPTED, ready-set, completion) and ACTS (fill/refill/recover/complete) as a loop extending /implement and the lanes-watchdog watch+signal, so the driver is ddflow itself. Today the watchdog act mode is per-decision default-off and the fill/recover/complete loop lives in the harness Kilo cron instead, so there is no in-repo scheduler: implement the native scheduler loop (extend /implement to a claim-implement-gates-merge-complete-next loop plus a monitor that fills idle lanes/reaps interrupted/accepts red), keeping refill demoted to the harness wave-driver per the autofill-is-harness-pattern decision. Natural extension of B4e2a112a97.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bd43790a326 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bd43790a326 --regression-test <test>` first).
